Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 – FAQ's

How to apply for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 online?

Visit your state's official WCD / ICDS portal (link provided in table above). Register with mobile & Aadhaar, fill the application form, upload documents (photo, 10th certificate, Aadhaar, domicile), and submit before the last date. Print the application acknowledgement slip after submission.

What is the eligibility for Anganwadi Worker 2026?

Candidates must have passed 10th or 12th standard from a recognized board. Age limit is 18–35 years (varies by state). Must be a permanent resident of the ward/village for which vacancy exists. Only female candidates are eligible for Worker and Helper posts.

What is the salary of Anganwadi Worker in 2026?

Anganwadi Worker receives a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000–₹20,000 depending on the state (Karnataka and TN are highest at ~₹14,000). Anganwadi Helper gets ₹5,000–₹7,000/month. The Central Government pays ₹4,500/month as base honorarium, and states add their own component on top.

Is there a written exam for Anganwadi jobs?

No, there is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Selection is purely merit-based on academic qualification marks (10th / 12th percentage). For Supervisor / CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted depending on the state.

What is the age limit for Anganwadi Helper?

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.

Forest Department Posts List

The forest department offers a range of posts across different levels, from ground-level field roles to gazetted officer positions. Eligibility for Forest Department Jobs 2026

Educational Qualification

  • Forest Guard / Forest Watcher / Field Guard: 10th or 12th pass from a recognized board
  • Forester: 12th pass, often with Science subjects; some states require a diploma in Forestry
  • Range Forest Officer: Graduate degree, frequently in Science, Agriculture, or Forestry
  • ACF / IFS: Graduate degree in a relevant discipline (Botany, Zoology, Forestry, Agriculture, Veterinary Science, Engineering, or Environmental Science), followed by the respective state or UPSC exam

Age Limit & Relaxation

The general age limit for Forest Guard and Forester posts is usually 18–27 years, though this varies by state. Age relaxation is generally available for SC/ST (5 years), OBC (3 years), PwBD candidates, and other reserved categories as per government norms.

Reservation & Age Relaxation for Ex-Servicemen

Most state forest departments reserve a fixed percentage of Forest Guard, Forester, and Beat Guard posts for ex-servicemen, in addition to SC, ST, OBC, and EWS reservations. Candidates applying for jobs for ex servicemen in forest department typically receive:

  • Additional age relaxation, usually 3–5 years beyond the general age cap (or as per length of military service)
  • Relaxed physical standards in several states
  • A reserved vacancy quota, separate from the general merit list

Exact quota percentages and relaxation norms differ by state, so always cross-check the specific notification before applying.

Physical Standards

Most Forest Guard and Forester posts require candidates to clear height, chest measurement (for male candidates), and a Physical Efficiency Test involving running, walking, or trekking - since the job involves regular field patrol duty in forest terrain.

Two Types of No Exam Govt Jobs

No-exam recruitment in India falls into two patterns, and knowing which one a notification belongs to tells you exactly what to prepare for:

Type Typical Posts Who it's for How Selection Works
Fresher - no exam, usually no interview Apprentice, GDS, trainee 10th/12th/ITI/Diploma/Graduate pass Merit list prepared from academic marks
Experienced - no exam, interview-based Officer, manager, specialist, medical Professionals with relevant work experience Shortlisting based on qualification/experience, followed by a personal interview

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Govt Jobs for Law Graduates - Eligibility (LLB, LLM, BL)

Eligibility varies by post, but the core requirement for almost every government law job is a recognised law degree. Senior and specialised roles add experience, an LLM, or Bar enrolment on top.

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor of Law (BL) / LLB (Legum Baccalaureus): the baseline qualification for most legal and law officer posts.
  • LLM (Master of Laws): required for senior legal officer, faculty, and some advisory positions.
  • Integrated 5-year degrees - BA LLB, BBA LLB, BCom LLB - are accepted wherever an LLB is required.

The degree must be from a university recognised by the Bar Council of India.

Bar Council Enrolment & AIBE

For litigation, prosecutor, and standing-counsel roles you generally need to be enrolled as an advocate with a State Bar Council, and many positions ask for the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) Certificate of Practice issued by the Bar Council of India. Purely advisory or research posts (Law Clerk, Research Fellow, Legal Consultant) often do not require enrolment.

Age Limit & Relaxations

The upper age limit is typically 30 to 40 years for the general category, depending on the post and recruiter. Statutory relaxations apply: usually 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC/ST, and additional relaxation for PwD and ex-servicemen candidates. Always confirm the exact limit and cut-off date in the official notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

Salary & Pay Scale for Government Law Jobs

Pay depends on the organisation and grade. Officer-level legal posts under the 7th Pay Commission generally fall in Pay Levels 10 to 12, with a monthly salary roughly between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500, plus Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, and other benefits. PSU legal officers are paid on IDA scales, which can be higher at entry grade.

Types of Law Officer / Legal Posts in Government Sector

  • Judicial Services - Civil Judge (Junior Division), Additional District Judge, High Court Judge, recruited via State Judicial Service Exams (PCS-J)
  • Law Officer / Legal Officer - Roles in public sector banks (IBPS SO Law), insurance companies (LIC AAO Legal), regulatory bodies (SEBI Grade A Legal), and PSUs (Coal India, NTPC, GAIL Legal)
  • Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor - Administrative legal support roles in ministries, universities, and district courts
  • Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO) - Prosecution roles recruited through State PSCs, requiring LLB and often a minimum years of practice

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, ADJ, High Court Judge)

Judicial Services is the most prestigious and highest-paying career path for LLB graduates. Recruitment happens through State Public Service Commissions (e.g., RPSC, UPPSC, MPPSC) via a three-stage exam: Preliminary, Mains, and Interview. Civil Judge posts typically require 0-3 years of practice depending on the state, while some states allow fresh LLB graduates to apply directly.

Law Officer / Legal Officer (Banks, PSU, Insurance)

Public sector banks and insurance companies recruit Law Officers through specialist officer (SO) exams. These posts require only an LLB degree (AIBE not mandatory) and offer competitive pay scales under the 7th Pay Commission equivalent structure, along with allowances.

Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor Posts

These are typically Group B/C administrative-legal posts in ministries, universities, and PSU legal departments, requiring an LLB degree and sometimes relevant drafting/litigation experience.

Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO)

APO recruitment is conducted by State PSCs (e.g., RPSC Assistant Prosecution Officer) and requires an LLB degree, enrollment as an advocate, and in most states, a minimum period of practice (often 3 years).

Selection Process for Law Govt Jobs

The selection process differs by post but commonly includes:

  1. Written examination - testing legal knowledge, aptitude, and general awareness (for judicial services and most exam-based posts).
  2. Interview / viva-voce - assessing legal reasoning and suitability.
  3. Document verification - degree, Bar enrolment, AIBE, age, and category certificates.

Advisory and consultant posts are often filled by shortlisting and interview alone, without a written exam.

How to Apply for Law Govt Jobs

  1. Find the post you are eligible for in the table above.
  2. Open the official notification and read the eligibility, fee, and important dates.
  3. Register on the recruiter's official portal.
  4. Fill in the application with your LLB/LLM, Bar enrolment, and personal details.
  5. Upload the required documents and photograph.
  6. Pay the application fee (if any) and submit before the last date.
  7. Save or print the confirmation for future reference.

Each row in the table links directly to the official notification, so you can apply from the source.

Law Govt Jobs FAQ's

What are the latest law govt jobs in 2026?

Current law government jobs in 2026 include Law Officer, Legal Officer, Assistant Prosecution Officer, Judicial Service, and Legal Adviser posts across High Courts, PSUs, public sector banks, and central/state departments. The table above is updated daily with vacancy count, last date, and the official notification link.

Which departments hire LLB and law graduates?

High Courts and District Courts, the Ministry of Law and Justice, UPSC, State Public Service Commissions, public sector banks, PSUs, insurance companies, and regulatory bodies regularly recruit law graduates for legal and judicial roles.

What is the eligibility for government law jobs?

Most posts require a Bachelor of Law (LLB/BL) from a recognised university; senior roles may require LLM and experience. Litigation and prosecutor posts usually require enrolment with a State Bar Council and, often, the AIBE certificate.

What is the salary of a Law Officer in the government sector?

A government Law Officer or Legal Officer typically earns between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500 per month under the 7th Pay Commission, depending on the organisation, plus DA, HRA, and allowances. PSU legal officers draw IDA-scale pay.

Can a fresher LLB graduate get a government job?

Yes. Freshers can apply for Civil Judge (Junior Division) judicial-service exams, Law Clerk and Research Fellow posts in High Courts, and trainee legal roles. Some PSU and bank Law Officer posts require a few years of post-enrolment experience.

How can I apply for law officer vacancies in central government?

Open the post in the table above, read the official notification, register on the recruiter's portal, fill in the application with your LLB and enrolment details, pay the fee, and submit before the last date.

What is the difference between Judicial Services and Law Officer posts

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, via state judiciary exams) places you on the bench as a judge. Law Officer/Legal Officer posts are departmental legal-counsel roles in PSUs, banks, and ministries - advisory and litigation support, recruited by interview or written test.

Is there an age limit for govt law jobs?

Most posts set the upper age at 30 to 40 years for the general category, with statutory relaxations for OBC, SC/ST, and PwD candidates. Check each notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026 - Download Link, Interview Dates & Full Details

The State Bank of India (SBI) has officially released the SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026 on 4 July 2026, and candidates who cleared the online examination for the Circle Based Officer (CBO) post can now download it from the official portal. As per the notice, the SBI CBO interview will be held from 13 July 2026 to 19 July 2026. If you're one of the shortlisted candidates, this is your final step before securing a role as a Circle Based Officer at SBI so let's walk through everything you need to know: where to download the call letter, what documents to carry, and how the final selection is calculated.

SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026 - Quick Overview

This section summarizes the most important facts about the SBI CBO 2026 interview round in one place, so you can quickly confirm the key dates and numbers without scrolling through the entire article.

Particulars Details
Recruiting Body State Bank of India (SBI)
Post Name Circle Based Officer (CBO)
Advertisement No. CRPD/CBO/2025-26/18
Total Vacancies 2,050
Interview Call Letter Release Date 4 July 2026
Interview Dates 13 July 2026 to 19 July 2026
Selection Stages Online Exam → Screening → Interview → Local Language Proficiency Test
Marks Allotted for Interview 50 Marks
Final Merit Weightage Online Test: 75% + Interview: 25%
Starting Basic Pay ₹48,480 + 2 Advance Increments

What Is the SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026?

Before downloading your admit card, it helps to understand exactly what this document is and why it matters for the recruitment process. The SBI CBO Interview Call Letter is the official admission ticket that confirms a candidate has cleared the earlier stages and is now eligible to appear for the personal interview round.

The interview call letter is a mandatory document for the SBI CBO Recruitment 2026 drive, which is being conducted to fill 2,050 vacancies for the Circle Based Officer post across various states and language zones. Without this call letter, candidates will not be permitted entry into the interview venue, so downloading and verifying it well in advance is essential.

SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026: Download Link

This section explains exactly where and how you can access your call letter online, along with what to do immediately after downloading it.

Candidates can download the SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026 through the official recruitment portal. Once downloaded, cross-check every detail printed on it including your interview date, reporting time, and venue address and keep both a printed copy and a digital backup ready ahead of interview day.

Click Here to Download SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026

Login Credentials Required to Download the Call Letter

To successfully access your call letter, you'll need specific login credentials that were created during your application process. This section lists exactly what you need to have on hand.

You will need the following details to log in to the portal:

  • Registration Number or Roll Number (generated at the time of application/exam)
  • Password or Date of Birth (as set/used during registration)

Since these credentials were generated earlier in the recruitment cycle, candidates who have misplaced them should retrieve their registration details before the download window gets busy closer to the interview dates.

How to Download SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026: Step-by-Step

If you're downloading your call letter for the first time, this simple step-by-step guide will help you complete the process without errors.

  1. Visit the official SBI website or the direct download link provided above.
  2. Navigate to the "Careers" section (if accessing via sbi.co.in).
  3. Click on the SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026 link.
  4. Enter your Registration Number/Roll Number and Password/Date of Birth.
  5. Click submit to view your call letter.
  6. Download the PDF and take a clear printout for the interview day.

Details Mentioned on the SBI CBO Interview Call Letter

Your call letter contains critical information you must verify immediately after downloading. This section breaks down exactly what's printed on the document.

The SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026 includes:

  • Candidate's name and roll number
  • Interview date and reporting time
  • Interview venue name and complete address
  • Important day-of instructions and guidelines

If any detail such as your name, photograph, or center address appears incorrect, contact the SBI recruitment cell or IBPS helpline immediately for correction.

Also Read: UP Home Guard DV/PST Admit Card 2026

Documents to Carry for the SBI CBO Interview 2026

Carrying the correct set of documents is non-negotiable for interview-day entry. This section lists everything you must bring along.

  • A printed copy of the interview call letter
  • A valid original photo ID proof (Aadhaar, PAN, Passport, Voter ID, etc.)
  • Original and photocopies of educational certificates and mark sheets
  • Recent passport-size photographs (the same one used during application, if specified)

Candidates should keep all documents organized in a single folder to avoid last-minute confusion at the venue.

SBI CBO 2026 Selection Process Explained

Understanding how your final selection is calculated helps you prepare strategically for the interview. This section explains the complete selection methodology for SBI CBO 2026.

The SBI Circle Based Officer recruitment follows a multi-stage selection process:

  1. Online Examination - The first screening stage testing candidates' aptitude and knowledge.
  2. Screening/Shortlisting - Candidates are shortlisted based on online exam performance for the interview stage.
  3. Interview - Worth 50 marks, assessing banking awareness, professional knowledge, and communication skills.
  4. Local Language Proficiency Test - Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in the regional/local language relevant to their applied state or circle.

How Is the Final Merit List Prepared?

The final selection isn't based on the interview alone it combines scores from multiple stages using a fixed weightage formula.

The final merit list for SBI CBO 2026 is prepared using combined weightage:

  • Online Examination: 75% weightage
  • Interview: 25% weightage

This means strong performance in the online exam significantly boosts your overall chances, but a good interview score remains essential for the final cutoff.

SBI CBO Salary and Pay Scale 2026

Many candidates preparing for the interview also want clarity on the compensation structure for this role.

Selected Circle Based Officers will receive a starting basic pay of ₹48,480, along with 2 advance increments, as per the official SBI CBO notification. For a full salary breakup including allowances and in-hand pay, refer to the SBI CBO Salary details.

SBI CBO Recruitment 2026: Background Details

A quick refresher on the recruitment cycle helps put the interview call letter in context for candidates tracking the full timeline.

Interview Dates 13-19 July 2026

The recruitment drive (Advt. No. CRPD/CBO/2025-26/18) targets 2,050 Circle Based Officer vacancies distributed across multiple states, with eligibility requiring a bachelor's degree in any stream along with knowledge of the local language of the respective state/circle applied for. The minimum age is 21 years and the maximum age is 30 years, as reckoned on 31 December 2025.

What to Do After the SBI CBO Interview?

Once your interview is complete, there are a few more stages before you receive your final appointment. Candidates should track official SBI communication for updates on Document Verification and Medical Examination, which typically follow the interview stage before the final selection and joining process.

UPSC Recruitment 2026 (Advt 07) – Selection Process

The selection process for UPSC Advertisement No. 07/2026 varies by post. For most posts, it consists of shortlisting based on the online application, followed by a Recruitment Test (RT) or Combined Recruitment Test (CRT) if warranted, and then a Personality Test (Interview). Candidates will be shortlisted for interview based on the information provided in their online application and their performance in the RT, if held.

  1. Online Application Submission: Submit application at upsconline.nic.in by 17 July 2026.
  2. Shortlisting: UPSC shortlists candidates on the basis of information provided in the online application. Incorrect information may lead to rejection through computer-based shortlisting.
  3. Recruitment Test (RT) / Combined Recruitment Test (CRT) – if applicable: For posts where the number of applications is large, UPSC may conduct an RT or CRT before the interview. The test is ordinarily conducted at the following centres: Ahmedabad, Bhopal, Chennai, Delhi, Dispur (Guwahati), Jaipur, Jammu, Kochi, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Port Blair, Ranchi, and Visakhapatnam.
  4. Personality Test / Interview: Shortlisted candidates are called for interview. Candidates must bring the printout of their online application and all original/self-attested copies of supporting documents.
  5. Final Selection and Appointment: Appointment orders are issued by the respective Ministry/Department. UPSC may grant higher initial pay to candidates adjudged meritorious at the interview stage.

Common Mistakes to Avoid – UPSC Advt 07/2026 Application

Given the large number of posts and the diverse eligibility conditions in UPSC Advertisement No. 07/2026, there are several common errors candidates make. Correcting these proactively can prevent outright rejection before the interview stage.

  • Applying for a post you do not meet the exact qualification for: UPSC shortlists strictly on the basis of declared qualifications. Applying with a "similar" or "equivalent" degree without a formal equivalence order from the competent authority is grounds for rejection. Produce the equivalence order if claiming an equivalent qualification.
  • Entering an inactive or incorrect e-mail address: UPSC sends all interview schedules and document requirements exclusively by e-mail. A wrong email means you will miss the interview call entirely. Double-check before submitting.
  • Submitting incomplete category documents later: All category-based claims (caste, disability, ex-serviceman) must be supportable at the interview stage with original documents in the prescribed UPSC proforma - not general certificates from hospitals or district offices.
  • Not declaring government service: Persons already in regular government service must submit a declaration to UPSC that they have informed their Head of Office in writing. Omitting this can lead to disciplinary consequences.
  • Attempting to withdraw the application after submission: UPSC explicitly states that candidates will not be allowed to withdraw their application once submitted. Apply only if you are genuinely eligible and intend to participate.
  • Bringing a mobile phone to the exam/interview venue: Mobile phones and all electronic devices are strictly banned at UPSC examination/interview halls - even in switched-off mode. Violation results in debarment from future examinations.
  • Waiting until the last day: The portal closes at exactly 1800 Hrs on 17 July 2026. Server congestion near the deadline is common. Complete your application at least 2–3 days in advance.
  • Submitting documents in a language other than Hindi/English without a notarised transcript: Any certificate in a regional language must be accompanied by a transcript attested by a Gazetted Officer or Notary.

Any officer in the Upper Division Grade of the Central Secretariat Clerical Service who, as on 01 July 2025, has rendered not less than six years' approved service in that grade is eligible to appear.

Eligibility for Ministry of External Affairs (Cadre Cell)

Officers in the Upper Division Clerk Grade of the MEA Service who, as on 01 July 2025, have (a) successfully completed such mandatory training programme(s) as prescribed by the Ministry of External Affairs and (b) rendered not less than six years' approved service in the grade are eligible.

Disqualification Conditions

A candidate who resigns, quits service, or whose services are terminated after applying will not be eligible for appointment on the result of this examination. Similarly, candidates appointed to an ex-cadre post or another service on "transfer" without a lien in the SSA/UDC grade are not eligible. This does not apply to candidates on deputation with the approval of the competent authority.

SSC ASO Apply Online 2026 – Step-by-Step Process

The SSC ASO Apply Online 2026 process involves two stages: One Time Registration (OTR) on the SSC portal, followed by filling the actual examination application. Candidates who had registered on the old website (ssc.nic.in) must create a fresh OTR on the new website (ssc.gov.in) as the old OTR is not functional on the new portal.

  1. Visit the official SSC website: https://ssc.gov.in
  2. Click on "Register Now" under the Login or Register section to complete One Time Registration (OTR) if not already done on the new website.
  3. During OTR, opt for Aadhaar-Based Authentication as advised by the Commission.
  4. After OTR is complete, log in using your Registration Number and password.
  5. Click the "Apply" link under "Assistant Section Officer / Assistant Grade Limited Departmental Competitive Examination, 2025" in the Live Exam tab.
  6. Fill in departmental details - select your Cadre/Service, joining date of feeder service, and length of service.
  7. Capture a live photograph using webcam/smartphone as prompted (no pre-existing photo allowed).
  8. Upload your scanned signature in JPEG format (10–20 KB, dimensions: 6 cm × 2 cm).
  9. Upload mandatory documents including certified true copy of Service Book (first page) and particulars of service. PwBD candidates must also upload their disability certificate.
  10. Review all entries in the Preview section, accept the declaration, and click Submit Application.
  11. Take a printout of the submitted application form.
  12. Submit the printed copy along with all required documents through your Head of Department / Head of Office to SSC (NR), New Delhi, by 23 July 2026.

Important: Only those candidates whose application is forwarded by their Head of Department / Head of Office will be considered for admission to this examination. Applications submitted directly without departmental forwarding will be rejected.

SSC ASO Exam Pattern 2026 – Scheme of Examination

The SSC Assistant Section Officer Exam 2026 is conducted in two parts. Part-I is a Computer Based Examination (CBE) carrying 300 marks, and Part-II involves Evaluation of Service Records (APARs) carrying 100 marks. The final merit is prepared on the combined aggregate of both parts. There is no separate qualifying exam - this is a competitive examination.

Part-I: Computer Based Examination (300 Marks)

Paper Subjects Type Max. Marks Duration
Paper-I (i) General Awareness – flagship programmes and GoI initiatives
(ii) Constitutional provisions and their general application in GoI
(iii) Parliamentary procedures (Manual of Parliamentary Procedures, MoPA instructions)
(iv) Reading Comprehension in English / Hindi
(v) Central Secretariat – Manual of Office Procedure
(vi) Allocation of Business Rules and Transaction of Business Rules
(vii) Noting and Drafting		 Objective (MCQ) 150 3 hours (4 hours for eligible scribe candidates)
Paper-II (i) Service Rules – Leave Rules, Conduct & CCA Rules, Pension and NPS Rules

(iii) Legislations – RTI Act 2005, POSH Act 2013
(iv) Records Management

There is a negative marking of 0.25 marks (25%) for each wrong answer in both Paper-I and Paper-II. Candidates must attempt the examination only in the language (English or Hindi) opted in the application form. There will be no question paper in Braille.

Part-II: Evaluation of Record of Service (100 Marks)

One hundred marks are reserved for evaluation of Annual Performance Appraisal Reports (APARs). Candidates shortlisted based on their Part-I aggregate performance will proceed to Part-II. Marks from Part-II will be added to determine the final rank. Once APARs have been evaluated, no request for change in APAR grading will be entertained.

SSC ASO Selection Process 2026

The SSC ASO selection process 2026 is a two-stage merit-based system. Candidates must clear the Computer Based Examination before their service records are evaluated. Final selection is strictly based on combined merit - no candidate has a right to selection merely by passing the exam.

  1. Stage 1 – Computer Based Examination (Part-I): Paper-I and Paper-II, each of 150 marks. The Commission may fix minimum qualifying marks individually for each paper.
  2. Stage 2 – APAR Evaluation (Part-II): Only candidates who qualify Part-I are eligible. Service records (APARs) are evaluated for 100 marks.
  3. Final Merit: Aggregate of Part-I (300 marks) + Part-II (100 marks) = 400 marks total. Names of finally selected candidates will be arranged in order of merit separately for each cadre.

Tie-Breaking Rules

In case of equal aggregate marks, ties are resolved in the following order: (i) Marks in Paper-I, (ii) Marks in Paper-II, (iii) Date of birth - older candidate ranked higher, (iv) Alphabetical order of names.

The SSC ASO pay scale is at Pay Level-7 in the 7th Pay Commission Pay Matrix, with a pay range of Rs. 44,900 to Rs. 1,42,400 per month. Common Mistakes to Avoid – SSC ASO Apply Online 2026

Based on typical departmental exam application processes, candidates should be especially careful about the following errors that frequently lead to rejection or disqualification.

  • Using Old SSC OTR: OTR created on the old website (ssc.nic.in) will not work on ssc.gov.in. Candidates must create a new OTR on the new website before applying.
  • Not forwarding hard copy through HoD/HoO: Online submission alone is not enough. The printed application must be forwarded by the Head of Department or Head of Office and must reach SSC NR by 23 July 2026. Failure to do this renders the application void.
  • Uploading pre-existing photographs: The portal requires a live photograph captured at the time of application. Uploading a pre-existing photo will lead to summary rejection.
  • Miniature or blurred signatures: Signatures must occupy at least 80% of the signature box and must be clear. Miniature signatures are the most common reason for rejection.
  • Mismatch in personal details: Name, date of birth, father's name, and mother's name in the application must exactly match the Matriculation certificate. Any discrepancy can cancel your candidature.
  • Submitting multiple applications: Only one application is allowed per candidate. Multiple submissions may lead to rejection of all applications.
  • Not verifying service eligibility before applying: Candidates must confirm they have completed six years of approved service in the feeder grade as on 01 July 2025 before applying.
  • Changing appearance before the exam: The appearance on exam day must match the photograph in the application form. Examination staff may deny entry to candidates with noticeably different appearances.
  • Carrying electronic devices: Mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, or any electronic gadget in the examination hall attracts a debarment of 3–5 years.

SSC SSA Eligibility Criteria 2026 - Who Can Apply

Length of Service Requirement

However, if the candidate was appointed to the LDC grade through a competitive examination (including a Limited Departmental Competitive Examination), the results of such examination must have been declared at least five years before the crucial date and the candidate must have rendered at least four years of approved and continuous service in that grade.

Typewriting Test Condition

Unless exempted, the candidate must have passed the typewriting test held by UPSC or SSC for confirmation in the Lower Division Clerk grade on or before the date of this notification. Candidates who have been granted exemption from the typewriting test must quote the order number and date of such exemption in the application form.

SSC SSA UDC Selection Process 2026

The final rank is based on the combined aggregate of both stages. Eligibility Criteria – Who Can Apply for SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025

This is a Limited Departmental Competitive Examination — it is NOT open to the general public. Only serving central government employees who meet specific service and educational conditions are eligible. The crucial date for determining eligibility is 1 August 2025. Candidates who have resigned, quit service, or whose services have been terminated after applying will not be eligible for appointment on the result of this examination.

Service Eligibility Conditions

  • Must be a permanent or regularly appointed temporary Group 'C' employee with Grade Pay of Rs. 1800.
  • Must have rendered not less than 3 years of regular service as a Group 'C' employee with Grade Pay of Rs. 1800 as on the crucial date of 1 August 2025.
  • A Group 'C' employee on deputation to an ex-cadre post with approval of competent authority is also eligible, if otherwise eligible.
  • A Group 'C' employee appointed to an ex-cadre post or another service on transfer who continues to have a lien in the Group 'C' post is also eligible, if otherwise eligible.
  • The parent Service/Cadre of the candidate must be a participating Service/Cadre of this examination.

Educational Qualification

  • Must have passed the 12th standard examination from a recognized Board or equivalent.

Typewriting Test Requirement

Candidates shall have to pass (if not already passed) one of the periodical typewriting tests in English or Hindi held by SSC:

Language Speed on Manual Typewriter Speed on Computer Key Depressions Per Hour (KDPH)

Hindi 25 words per minute (wpm) 30 wpm 9,000 KDPH

Note: Candidates who do not pass the typewriting test within the probation period are liable to be reverted. Candidates declared permanently unfit for typewriting by a Civil Surgeon due to physical disability may be exempted in consultation with DoPT.

Disqualification Condition

A candidate who after applying — or after appearing in the examination — resigns, quits service, severs connection, or whose services are terminated will not be eligible for appointment. This rule does not apply to candidates on approved deputation to an ex-cadre post.

Application Fee – SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025

This is consistent with the nature of a Limited Departmental Competitive Examination where serving government employees are the applicants. However, candidates may note that representation/objection on answer keys, if any, requires a fee of Rs. 50/- per question (non-refundable), payable online through the Commission's challenge/objection system.

Selection Process – SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 Exam Pattern

The SSC JSA LDC LDCE 2025 selection process consists of a single-stage Computer Based Examination (CBE) of 180 marks and 3 hours duration. There is no interview or skill test at the selection stage. Final merit is determined solely on the basis of aggregate performance in the CBE, and the Commission prepares a Select List in order of merit up to the number of vacancies.

Part-I: Computer Based Examination (CBE) – Exam Pattern

Subject Number of Questions Maximum Marks
Comprehension / General English 60 60
General Knowledge 60 60
CSMOP (Central Secretariat Manual of Office Procedure) 60 60
Total 180 180
  • Duration: 3 hours (4 hours for candidates eligible for scribe)
  • Question Type: Objective type, Multiple Choice
  • Negative Marking: 0.25 marks deducted for each wrong answer
  • Medium: Candidates must attempt in the language (English/Hindi) opted in the application form, except the "General English" section which must be attempted in English
  • No Braille Question Paper: There is no Question Paper in Braille for Visually Handicapped candidates
  • Exam Centre: Delhi-NCR only
  • Compensatory Time: 20 minutes per hour for candidates eligible for scribe/assistive devices

Syllabus for Computer Based Examination

Comprehension (English/Hindi) and General English Simple composition, Applied Grammar

Tie-Breaking Rules

When two or more candidates secure equal aggregate marks, the tie is resolved in the following order:

  1. Marks obtained in 'Comprehension and General English' subject of CBE
  2. Marks obtained in 'General Knowledge' subject of CBE
  3. Date of birth — older candidate ranked higher
  4. Alphabetical order of names

Select List Preparation

After the examination, names of finally selected candidates will be arranged by SSC in order of merit. Selected candidates will be recommended for inclusion in the Select List for JSA/LDC Grade of CSCS Cadre up to the required number of vacancies. This is a competitive examination — success does not confer an automatic right to selection unless the cadre authority also confirms suitability based on conduct in service.

SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 Apply Online – Step-by-Step Process

The SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 apply online process is available exclusively at https://ssc.gov.in. This is a two-part process — One-Time Registration (OTR) followed by the Online Application Form. After submission, eligible candidates must also ensure their department forwards the printed hard copy to SSC Northern Region by 23 July 2026. Only applications forwarded by the Head of Department/Head of Office will be considered for admission.

  1. One-Time Registration (OTR) on the NEW SSC website: If you have not yet completed OTR on https://ssc.gov.in, do so first. OTR done on the old website (ssc.nic.in) is NOT valid for the new portal. Keep ready: mobile number, email ID, Aadhaar number (or Voter ID/PAN/Passport/Driving License), and Matriculation (10th class) board/roll number/year of passing. Opt for Aadhaar-Based Authentication for smoother processing. Complete OTR registration within 14 days of starting, or data will be deleted. Save your Registration Number and password.
  2. Log in and apply for the examination: Visit https://ssc.gov.in, log in with your Registration Number and password, click "Apply" under the JSA/LDC LDCE 2025 (CSCS, DoPT) listing in the "Live Exam" section.
  3. Fill the Online Application Form: Personal details (S. No. 1–18) auto-populate from OTR. Fill in cadre (Central Secretariat Clerical Service, DoPT), examination year (2025), joining date of feeder service/cadre, length of service, exam medium (English or Hindi), ministry/department/office details, Head of Department and Head of Office details, and complete service history in chronological order.
  4. Upload photograph (live capture) and signature: Capture a live photograph directly through the application module — no pre-existing photograph is required. Ensure plain background, good lighting, no cap/mask/glasses. Upload scanned signature in JPEG format (10–20 KB), dimensions approx. 6.0 cm (width) × 2.0 cm (height). Blurred or miniature signatures lead to rejection.
  5. Upload required certificates: Upload the following in PDF/JPEG format: (i) Service Book first page certified true copy attested by HoD/HoO; (ii) Certified particulars of service (posts held, pay scale, capacity); (iii) Educational qualification certificate (12th standard or equivalent); (iv) Disability certificate (PwBD candidates only).
  6. Preview, declare, and submit: Use the Preview option to verify all entries. Check photograph and signature compliance. Click "I Agree" on the declaration and submit. On successful submission, take a printout of the application form.
  7. Forward hard copy through department (mandatory): Print the submitted application form and attach self-attested photocopies of supporting documents. Submit to your Head of Department/Head of Office for forwarding to: The Regional Director, Staff Selection Commission (Northern Region), Block No.12, C.G.O. Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi – 110003, so as to reach by 23 July 2026 at 6:00 PM (or 30 July 2026 for candidates abroad/Andaman & Nicobar/Lakshadweep).
  8. Download Admit Card: Admission Certificate (AC) will be uploaded on the SSC-NR website (https://sscnr.nic.in) approximately 10 days before the exam; available for download 3–4 days before the exam. AC will NOT be sent by post.

Important: Only applications forwarded by the Head of Department/Head of Office will be considered. Candidates are advised to submit to their department well before the closing date to ensure timely forwarding. Applications received after the closing date at SSC will be summarily rejected.

Documents Required – Upload Checklist & Hard Copy Submission

Candidates applying for the SSC LDC JSA LDCE 2025 DoPT must upload the following documents at the time of online application and also include self-attested photocopies with the printed application forwarded by the department. All documents must be clear and legible; no original documents should be submitted at this stage.

Documents to Upload Online (and attach with hard copy)

  • Certified true copy of first page of Service Book duly attested by Head of Department/Head of Office — showing name, father's name, husband's name (if applicable), nationality, SC/ST details (if applicable), date of birth in Christian Era (figures and words)
  • Certified particulars of service attested by HoD/HoO — showing posts held, scale of pay, and capacity (substantive/officiating/permanent/temporary)
  • Certificate of essential educational qualification (12th standard or equivalent), if applicable
  • Disability certificate (PwBD candidates) — as per Annexure-VII (Form-V) or Annexure-VIII (Form-VI for multiple disabilities) of the notification

Documents to Carry to Exam Centre

  • Hard copy of Admission Certificate (AC)
  • Departmental Identity Card (Original) issued by employer
  • At least one valid government-issued photo ID — Voter ID, Driving License, PAN Card, Passport, or any Central/State Government-issued photo ID card (for candidates who have not undergone Aadhaar-Based Authentication, also carry two recent passport-size colour photographs and an additional DOB proof)
  • If Photo ID does not show date of birth — carry Matriculation Certificate/Marks Sheet (issued by CBSE/ICSE/State Boards), Birth Certificate, or Category Certificate
  • PwBD candidates availing scribe/assistive devices — carry Medical Certificate (Annexure-II or III) and scribe's photo ID proof (original and photocopy)

Departmental Forwarding Certificate – Role of Head of Department

A unique feature of the SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 is the mandatory role of the Head of Department or Head of Office in the application process. The forwarding authority must certify the candidate's service particulars, verify eligibility, sign and stamp the photograph on the printed application, and forward it to SSC Northern Region by the deadline. Without this forwarding, no application will be considered.

The Head of Department/Office must certify the following key points (as per Annexure-VI of the notification):

  • All information given by the candidate is verified and correct as per service records
  • The candidate belongs to the SC/ST community (if claimed), as verified from service records
  • No circumstance renders the candidate unsuitable for promotion to JSA/LDC of CSCS Cadre, DoPT
  • The candidate is a regularly appointed temporary/permanent Group 'C' employee of the participating Ministry/Department/Organization
  • The candidate fulfills all eligibility conditions for the year 2025 considering the crucial date and length of service
  • The candidate has not been debarred or disqualified by any Public Service Commission/SSC/Subordinate Service Commission for any examination/selection
  • A vacancy in the appropriate category is available in the Department/Organization

Critical: The forwarding authority must also sign the candidate's photograph on the printed application form and put a half-seal on the photograph and half on the form. Without this, the application will be summarily rejected.

PwBD / Scribe Provisions – SSC JSA LDC LDCE 2025

Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) applying for the SSC JSA LDC DoPT LDCE 2025 can avail the facility of scribe, technology, or assistive devices. The eligibility for scribe assistance depends on the nature and percentage of disability. Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour of examination will be provided to all candidates eligible for scribe assistance — whether or not they actually avail the facility.

  • Blindness and Cerebral Palsy (40%+): Scribe/technology/assistive devices provided on request in the application form, with upload of disability certificate.
  • Other PwBD categories: Scribe provided on production of a certificate from Chief Medical Officer/Civil Surgeon/Medical Superintendent of a Government health institution (as per Annexure-II) confirming physical limitation to write.
  • PwD with less than 40% disability having difficulty writing: Scribe provided as per OM No. 29-6/2019-DD-III dated 10.08.2022, on production of certificate as per Annexure-III.
  • Scribe/assistive device facility must be opted for in the online application form — it will not be provided without prior intimation.

Common Mistakes to Avoid – SSC JSA LDC LDCE 2025 DoPT Application

This is a departmental exam with additional procedural requirements not seen in open competitive exams. Many candidates lose their application due to easily avoidable errors. Here are the most critical mistakes to watch for in the SSC JSA LDC CSCS DoPT LDCE 2025:

  1. Using old SSC website OTR for the new website: OTR generated on the old website (ssc.nic.in) is NOT valid on the new website (ssc.gov.in). Candidates must generate a fresh OTR on the new portal. Using old OTR credentials leads to failure to apply.
  2. Not completing OTR within 14 days: If you start OTR registration but do not complete it within 14 days, your data is automatically deleted. Start and complete OTR well before the application deadline.
  3. Submitting multiple applications: Only ONE application should be submitted. Multiple applications may lead to rejection of the entire candidature.
  4. Not ensuring the department forwards the hard copy on time: Many candidates submit the online application correctly but forget that the department must also forward the printed hard copy to SSC NR by 23 July 2026. Applications received late at SSC — even with valid online submissions — are summarily rejected. Inform your department immediately after applying online.
  5. Forwarding authority not signing the photograph: The Head of Department/Office must personally sign the candidate's photo on the printed application form and put a half-seal across the photo. Without this, the application is summarily rejected — no appeal entertained.
  6. Uploading a photograph of a pre-existing photograph: The application module captures a live photograph. Candidates who photograph a pre-existing printed photo (instead of taking a live capture) will have their applications rejected summarily.
  7. Wearing glasses, cap, or mask in the live photograph: Candidates are specifically instructed not to wear any of these while capturing the live photo. Similarly, the appearance at the exam should match the application photo — changed appearances may deny entry.
  8. Uploading a miniature or blurred signature: The signature must be in JPEG format (10–20 KB), approximately 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm, occupying at least 80% of the signature box. Miniature or blurred signatures are a leading cause of application rejection.
  9. Not indicating the correct medium of examination: Candidates must choose English or Hindi as the medium in the application. The General English section must be attempted in English regardless of medium chosen. This choice cannot be changed after submission.
  10. Changing appearance significantly between application and exam day: Since the exam centre staff verifies appearance against the application photo, significant changes (beard, haircut, spectacles) may raise suspicion and lead to not being allowed to appear.

Who Can Apply for CSIR ASO Recruitment 2026?

Only candidates who hold a University degree and are non-recommended candidates of CSE-2024, as per the list available on the UPSC Pratibha Setu Portal, are eligible to apply. Candidates not meeting this condition need not apply.

  • Age Limit: Not exceeding 33 years as on the closing date of online application
  • Age Relaxation: SC/ST - 5 years; OBC (NCL) - 3 years; PwBD (UR) - 10 years; PwBD (SC/ST) - 15 years; PwBD (OBC) - 13 years; Ex-Servicemen - 3 years after deducting actual military service; CSIR Departmental candidates - 5 years

CSIR ASO Application Fee

UR, OBC (NCL), EWS Categories Rs. 500
Women / SC / ST / PwBD / Ex-Servicemen NIL

CSIR ASO Selection Process 2026

Selection is based on shortlisting followed by a qualifying computer test, not a fresh written exam. Candidates will be screened using their existing CSE-2024 scores before appearing for the Computer Proficiency Test.

  • Candidates are shortlisted in a 1:5 ratio (5 times the vacancies per category) based on total marks (Mains + Personality Test) obtained in UPSC's CSE-2024
  • Shortlisted candidates must appear for the Computer Proficiency Test (CPT) - qualifying in nature, 100 marks, 1-hour duration, covering Word Processing, Spreadsheets, and PowerPoint
  • CPT qualifying threshold: UR - 40%, EWS - 37%, OBC - 37%, SC - 35%, ST - 35%, PwBD (all categories) - 30%
  • CPT will be conducted in Delhi (tentatively; CSIR may conduct it elsewhere)
  • Final selection is based on total CSE-2024 marks (Mains + Personality Test), subject to qualifying the CPT
  • A single merit list is prepared; cadre allocation (General/Finance & Accounts/Stores & Purchase) is decided by CSIR based on merit and candidate preference, and once allotted is final

How to Apply for CSIR ASO Recruitment 2026

  • Visit www.csir.res.in or recruitment.csir.res.in
  • Click on "Apply Online" and register using your UPSC Roll Number, email ID, and mobile number
  • Note the User ID and password sent to your registered email/mobile
  • Log in and complete the profile page (Gender, DOB, Marital Status, Category, PwBD status, Ex-Servicemen status, etc.) - once locked, details cannot be modified
  • Fill all 6 tabs: Apply, Personal Details, Education, Experience, Additional Details, Uploads
  • Upload scanned photograph (jpg, <50 KB), signature (jpg, <50 KB), and required certificates (pdf, <1 MB each)
  • Preview and verify the application, then click Submit
  • Pay the applicable fee via SBI Collect (if applicable) and upload the e-Receipt before the last date
  • Take a printout of the final submitted application for future reference

How to Apply Online

Candidates must apply online only through the TMB careers portal at www.ib.tmbonline.bank.in/tmb_careers/. No other mode of submission will be accepted by the Bank.

  1. Download and Read the Advertisement – Before applying, go through the detailed advertisement by clicking "Download Advertisement" under the title "Recruitment Advertisement" on the careers portal, and confirm your eligibility for the post.
  2. Register on the Portal – Log on to the Bank’s website, click "Apply Online," and register for the appropriate post using a valid personal email ID and contact number, which should remain active till completion of the recruitment process.
  3. Activate Your Registration – On successful registration, an activation link will be sent to the registered email ID, and a Registration Number and Password will be sent to the registered mobile number. Candidates should note these details carefully, as they cannot proceed without them.
  4. Log In and Fill the Application – Click the activation link to reach the Careers portal, then log in using the Registration Number/Username and Password. Fill in all details carefully, using "Save/Continue" on each page. Ensure the candidate’s name and father’s/husband’s name are spelt exactly as per certificates/mark sheets, as any discrepancy may lead to disqualification.
  5. Upload Photograph, Signature & Documents – Upload the photograph (390 x 520 pixels, max 120 KB) and signature (240 x 240 pixels, max 60 KB, not in capital letters), along with the required enclosures listed in the Documents Required section (each max 250 KB).
  6. Submit the Application – Click "Confirm/Submit" at the bottom of the page. A message confirming "Registration is successful" will be displayed, and a copy of the system-generated application form will be emailed to the registered address. Candidates should take a printout for future reference.

Important Instructions

  • Canvassing in any form will result in disqualification.
  • The job role and location are subject to transfer based on the Bank’s requirements.
  • The application should reach the Bank on or before 18 July 2026.
  • Candidates must adhere strictly to the eligibility conditions given; any wrong information, or a candidate found ineligible at any stage of the process or later, will result in disqualification.
  • E-applications with incorrect or incomplete particulars, or without the required certificate copies attached, are liable to be rejected.
  • The Bank reserves the right to reject any application without assigning any reason, and the Bank’s decision on eligibility, interview, and selection will be final. The Bank also reserves the right to eliminate ineligible candidates at any point before, during, or after the personal interview/selection.
  • E-applications will be scrutinized, and shortlisted applicants will be communicated individually by post/email with interview details. No correspondence in this regard will be entertained by the Bank.

RRB Technician Selection Process 2026

Candidates often ask how RRB selects Technicians, and the answer is a three-stage process based purely on merit. The recruitment involves a Computer Based Test (CBT), Document Verification (DV), and a Medical Examination, with shortlisting at each stage determined by performance in the previous one.

  1. Computer Based Test (CBT): A single CBT of 90 minutes with 100 questions and negative marking of 1/3rd mark per wrong answer. Minimum qualifying marks are 40% (UR/EWS), 30% (OBC-NCL/SC), and 25% (ST).
  2. Document Verification (DV): Candidates are shortlisted at a 1:1 ratio against vacancies based on CBT merit, RRB-wise. Original documents must be produced; no extra time is given for missing certificates.
  3. Medical Examination (ME): Conducted by Railway Medical Authorities as per the medical standard (A3, B1, B2, or C1) prescribed for the specific post.

Based on typical RRB recruitment cycles, CBT is expected a few months after the application closes, followed by DV and medical examination in subsequent phases - though exact dates will be announced on official RRB websites.

The Indian Air Force has released two separate recruitment notifications inviting online applications for Agniveervayu Intake 02/2027 (under the Agnipath Scheme) and Airmen Group 'Y' (Non-Technical) Medical Assistant Trade for Intake 02/2027. Online registration for both notifications opens on 06 July 2026 and closes on 26 July 2026, with the online examination scheduled for 22-23 September 2026. While Agniveervayu is open to unmarried male and female Indian candidates for a four-year engagement, the Airmen Medical Assistant trade is open only to male Indian/Gorkha (Nepal) candidates for a 20-year regular cadre tenure. Applications must be submitted through the official CASB portal at iafrecruitment.edcil.co.in.

IAF Agniveervayu Intake 02/2027 - Eligibility Criteria

Agniveervayu eligibility is divided across age, marital status, and educational qualification requirements specific to Science and Non-Science streams.

Age Limit for Agniveervayu

Candidates born between 01 July 2005 and 01 January 2010 (both dates inclusive) are eligible to apply. If a candidate clears all stages of selection, the upper age limit on the date of enrolment must not exceed 22 years.

Marital Status (Agniveervayu)

Only unmarried male and female candidates are eligible. Candidates must undertake not to marry during the four-year engagement period; female candidates must additionally undertake not to become pregnant during this period, as pregnancy or marriage during service can lead to dismissal.

Educational Qualification for Agniveervayu

Stream Qualification Required
Science Subjects 10+2/Intermediate with Maths, Physics & English (50% aggregate + 50% in English) OR 3-year Diploma in Engineering (Mechanical/Electrical/Electronics/Automobile/Computer Science/Instrumentation/IT) with 50% marks OR 2-year Vocational Course with Physics & Maths (50% marks)
Other than Science 10+2/Intermediate in any stream (50% aggregate + 50% in English) OR 2-year Vocational Course (50% aggregate + 50% in English)

Candidates eligible under Science Subjects may also opt to appear for both Science and Other-than-Science papers in a single sitting while registering.

Domicile Categories for Agniveervayu

Candidates must select one domicile category at the time of registration, which cannot be changed later, as shortlisting and the Provisional Select List are prepared state-wise:

  • Permanent Domicile: Permanent residents of districts of the State/UT, supported by a Domicile Certificate from a Gazetted Revenue Officer.
  • COAFP-I: Children of currently serving Air Force personnel posted in the relevant State/UT.
  • COAFP-II: Children of retired/discharged/deceased Air Force personnel residing in the State/UT for a minimum of one year.

  • Diploma/Pharmacy Route: Passed 10+2/Intermediate with PCB & English (50% aggregate, 50% English) PLUS a Diploma/B.Pharma/B.Sc in Pharmacy with minimum 50% marks, along with valid registration from the State Pharmacy Council or Pharmacy Council of India (PCI) at the time of enrolment.

IAF Recruitment 2026 - Stipend & Benefits

Pay structures differ significantly between the two postings, reflecting their different service models - Agniveervayu under the Agnipath Scheme versus a regular 20-year Airmen cadre.

Year Monthly Package In-Hand (70%) Agniveer Corpus Contribution GoI Contribution

They are not entitled to gratuity, pension, or Provident Fund contributions, and do not receive Ex-Servicemen (ESM) status after discharge. Up to 25% of each batch may be offered the opportunity to apply for the regular Airmen cadre based on performance.

  • Training Stipend: ₹14,600 per month during training.
  • Post-Training Salary: Starting gross emoluments of minimum ₹26,900 per month (including Military Service Pay), plus applicable Dearness Allowance.
  • Other Allowances: Transport Allowance, CPMA, Leave Ration Allowance, Children Education Allowance, HRA, and more.
  • Leave: 60 days annual leave + 30 days casual leave per calendar year.
  • Insurance: Group Insurance cover of ₹62.5 lakh at a premium of ₹3,200/month.
  • Job Role: Training in nursing and first-aid, management of medical stores/dispensaries, and ward supervision duties.

IAF Selection Process 2026: Exam Pattern

Both posts follow a three-phase selection process - an online written test, physical/adaptability tests, and a final medical examination.

Phase I: Online Written Test

Post/Stream Duration Subjects
Agniveervayu (Science) 60 minutes Physics, Mathematics, English
Agniveervayu (Other than Science) 45 minutes English, Reasoning & General Awareness
Agniveervayu (Both Streams) 85 minutes Physics, Mathematics, English, RAGA
Airmen Medical Assistant 45 minutes English, Reasoning & General Awareness

Marking Scheme (both posts): +1 mark for each correct answer, 0 for unattempted questions, and -0.25 for each wrong answer. Marks may be normalised to adjust for variation in difficulty across exam sessions, and candidates must qualify in each subject/paper individually.

Phase II: Physical Fitness & Adaptability Tests

Shortlisted candidates undergo the Physical Fitness Test (detailed above) followed by two written Adaptability Tests assessing suitability for military life and ability to adjust to Air Force working conditions and environments.

Phase III: Medical Examination

Candidates who clear Adaptability Test-II undergo a detailed medical examination by the Air Force Medical Team, including blood haemogram, urine tests, biochemistry profile (blood sugar, cholesterol, kidney & liver function), chest X-ray, and ECG. Candidates declared unfit may appeal via an Appeal Medical Board by depositing ₹40.

How to Apply for IAF Agniveervayu/Airmen Recruitment 2026

Applications must be submitted entirely online in two steps through the CASB portal.

  1. Visit the official portal: iafrecruitment.edcil.co.in
  2. Step I (Registration): Enter personal and contact details, then click "Generate OTP." Verify both mobile number and email ID using the OTPs received.
  3. Agree to the terms & conditions, re-verify entered details, and click "Submit" to receive your User ID and Password via email/SMS.
  4. Step II (Application Form): Log in and click "Go To Application" to fill in personal, communication, and qualification details.
  5. Upload scanned photograph, signature, parent's signature (if under 18), and left thumb impression as per specified size/format guidelines.
  6. Capture a live photo via webcam for face-match verification.
  7. Preview the form, correct any errors, and click "Submit."
  8. Pay the examination fee of ₹550 + 18% GST through the payment gateway.
  9. Print and retain a copy of the final submitted application form for future reference.

Candidates must indicate five preferred examination city choices while filling the application. Once submitted, the application cannot be withdrawn, and the fee is non-refundable.

Sangli DCC Bank Clerk Eligibility Criteria 2026

Understanding the eligibility criteria is the first step before applying. This section covers educational qualifications, domicile requirements, and other key conditions.

To be considered for the Junior Assistant role, candidates must fulfil all of the following conditions as on the date of application:

Educational Qualification

  • A graduate degree in any discipline from a recognized university.
  • Additionally, candidates must hold an MS-CIT certificate or an equivalent computer course recognized by the Government of Maharashtra (as per Govt. letter no. 277/39 dated 4 Feb. 2013). Accepted equivalents include D.O.A.C.C. and N.E.I.L.L.I.T. New Delhi certificates.
  • Exception: Candidates who are Graduates or Post-Graduates in Computer Science / Information Technology (IT) are exempt from the MS-CIT requirement.

Domicile Requirement

Domicile of Sangli District is mandatory. Candidates must submit a valid domicile certificate at the time of application. As per a Maharashtra Government resolution dated 08/05/2026, 70% of seats are reserved for Sangli District domiciles and 30% are open for candidates from other districts. However, if candidates from other districts are unavailable, those seats will be filled from Sangli domiciles.

Sangli DCC Bank Clerk Age Limit 2026

Age eligibility is calculated as of a specific reference date. Here's what you need to know:

  • Minimum Age: 18 years
  • Maximum Age: 35 years
  • Reference Date: 20/06/2026
  • Candidates must have been born not earlier than 21/06/1991 to be eligible.

Age relaxation, if any, will be governed by applicable rules; candidates should check the official notification for the latest updates.

Sangli DCC Bank Clerk Salary & Probation Details 2026

One of the most searched queries around this recruitment is the salary structure. Here's a breakdown:

During the 12-month probation period, selected clerks will receive a monthly stipend of ₹22,000/-. After successful completion of probation, the candidate will be placed in the bank's regular Clerk grade and will receive full emoluments as per the bank clerk pay scale.

Confirmation into regular service will depend on satisfactory assessment of work performance, attendance records, and confidential reports during the probation period.

The selection process for the Junior Assistant post involves two stages. Understanding this process helps candidates prepare strategically.

Stage 1: Online Examination
All shortlisted applicants will appear for an online computer-based test.

Stage 2: Personal Interview
Candidates who meet the cut-off in the online exam and whose educational documents are verified will be called for a personal interview conducted at Sangli.

The final merit list will be prepared in descending order based on scores obtained across both stages combined.

Sangli DCC Bank Clerk Apply Online 2026

The application process is entirely online. No offline or postal applications will be accepted. Follow the step-by-step guide below to complete your registration without errors.

Sangli DCC Bank Clerk Online Application 2026 – Step-by-Step

Step 1: Visit sanglidccb.bank.in/career and click "APPLY ONLINE".

Step 2: Select "Click here for New Registration" and enter your name, contact details, and email ID. A provisional registration number and password will be generated and sent via email/SMS.

Step 3: Log in and fill in all required fields carefully. Use "SAVE AND NEXT" to save your progress between sessions.

Step 4: Upload scanned copies of your:

  • Photograph (4.5cm × 3.5cm, colour, 20–50 KB, JPG format)
  • Signature (black ink, 140×60 pixels, 10–20 KB)
  • Left Thumb Impression (240×240 pixels, 20–50 KB)
  • Hand-Written Declaration (in English, black ink, 800×400 pixels, 50–100 KB)

Step 5: Preview all entries carefully before clicking "COMPLETE REGISTRATION"- no changes are allowed after this.

Step 6: Pay the application fee of ₹1,000 + ₹180 (18% GST) = ₹1,180/- online using Debit Card, Credit Card, Net Banking, IMPS, or Mobile Wallets.

Step 7: Save/print the e-Receipt. Applications are not registered until both the photograph and signature are successfully uploaded.

Important: Application fees are non-refundable. Once submitted, applications cannot be withdrawn or modified.

This update comes through an official notification dated 1 July 2026, issued by the bank's Human Capital Management (Recruitment & Promotion Division) at its Central Office in Mumbai.

When Is the Central Bank of India Apprentice Exam 2026?

Candidates who registered for this recruitment drive want a direct answer to one question: when exactly is the exam? According to the bank's official notification, the written examination for the Engagement of Apprentices under the Apprentices Act, 1961, for FY 2026-27 will be conducted on 5 July 2026, which falls on a Sunday. The exam will be conducted by the BFSI Sector Skill Council (BFSI SSC), the designated agency responsible for administering the test on behalf of Central Bank of India.

This confirms and follows up on the bank's earlier notification dated 11 June 2026, in which applications were first invited for the apprentice engagement process.

Central Bank of India Apprentice Eligibility Criteria 2026

Understanding the eligibility requirements is essential before appearing for the exam or checking your application status. Candidates applying for the Central Bank of India Apprentice post are required to meet basic educational and age-related criteria along with regional language knowledge.

  • Educational Qualification: Candidates must hold a Bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognized university.
  • Language Requirement: Candidates should possess knowledge of the local language of the region/state for which they are applying.
  • Age Limit (as on 31 May 2026): Minimum age of 20 years and maximum age of 28 years. Post-wise age relaxation details are available in the official notification.

Selection Process for Central Bank of India Apprentice 2026

Knowing the full selection process helps candidates prepare for each stage that follows the written exam. Central Bank of India follows a multi-stage selection procedure for apprentice engagement.

The selection process consists of the following stages:

  1. Written Examination - conducted by BFSI SSC on 5 July 2026
  2. Local Language Test - to verify proficiency in the regional language of the applied state
  3. Document Verification - verification of educational and identity documents
  4. Medical Examination - to confirm medical fitness for the apprenticeship

Merely meeting the eligibility criteria does not guarantee a call for the examination, interview, or selection process, as clarified in the bank's official notification.

Eligibility for RBI Site Engineer Recruitment 2026 is reckoned as on 01 June 2026 and includes nationality, age, educational qualification, and work experience requirements specific to each post. Post Essential Qualification Essential Work Experience

Consultant Site Engineer (Civil) Level 3 B.Tech or equivalent in Civil stream Min. 15 years in construction & project management, incl. 5 years in CPWD/CPSU/similar govt. org. not below Executive Engineer rank

RBI Site Engineer Selection Process 2026

Candidates wondering about the RBI Site Engineer selection process can note that there is no written exam for this recruitment. Selection happens through preliminary screening by a Screening Committee, followed by document verification and a personal interview.

Step-by-Step Selection Methodology

  • Screening & Shortlisting: The Screening Committee may enhance minimum qualification or experience criteria to limit the number of candidates called, in proportion to the number of vacancies. Merely meeting minimum eligibility does not guarantee an interview call.
  • Interview Call Letter: Shortlisted candidates receive their call letter only via email from [email protected] — no postal call letters are issued.
  • Document Verification: Candidates must produce up-to-date Experience Certificates clearly stating nature of duties, dates, duration, level/position, and responsibilities, along with category, age, and qualification proofs.
  • Interview: Candidates discuss their anticipated compensation (within the advertised range) along with previous employer compensation details before the interview, which is considered by the Selection Committee.
  • Final Selection: The RBI Services Board's decision on eligibility, shortlisting, and interview results is final and binding, with no further correspondence entertained.
